themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked dramatically to 93 THIS WEEK—a 459% increase over the 8-week baseline of 16.6 per week—alongside a 1900% spike in dangling street signs (5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average) and 433% spike in damaged street signs (4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 average), suggesting a sudden, widespread deterioration in road and signage conditions across Riverdale.
evidence: Street Condition complaints: 93 THIS WEEK vs. 16.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 11.75)
Dangling street signs: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 7.18, 1900% spike)
Damaged street signs: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 3.92, 433% spike)
Community Board budget request for traffic/pedestrian safety improvements suggests chronic infrastructure underfunding
reporting_angles: Site visit to document current street conditions and identify common infrastructure failures across multiple neighborhoods
Interview DOT to determine root cause—is this weather-related, deferred maintenance, or a specific incident triggering multiple complaints?
Investigate whether 298 recent DOB permits (particularly 181 alterations) correlate with temporary street damage or utility work

themes_detail.label: Noise Surge (Street & Construction)
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints THIS WEEK have exploded across two categories: Street/Sidewalk noise jumped 342% to 21 complaints THIS WEEK (vs. 4.8 weekly average), and Commercial noise spiked 259% to 13 complaints LAST WEEK (vs. 3.6 weekly average), while General Construction/Plumbing complaints jumped 182% to 12 THIS WEEK (vs. 4.2 average), suggesting either coordinated construction activity or a major noise-generating incident.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk: 21 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.8, 342% spike)
Noise - Commercial: 13 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.0, 259% spike)
General Construction/Plumbing: 12 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.04, 182% spike)
63 new building permits filed in last 90 days may indicate active construction across district
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaints spatially to pinpoint neighborhoods with heaviest concentration—is it isolated or district-wide?
Cross-reference with DOB permit database to identify active construction sites that may require enforcement of noise restrictions
Interview residents in affected blocks about timing and duration of noise to determine if complaints point to specific project(s)

themes_detail.label: Trash & Disposal Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Residential Disposal complaints spiked 276% to 8 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO (vs. 2.1 weekly average), and Sanitation Worker/Vehicle complaints hit an anomalous peak of 3 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO (vs. 0.4 weekly average, 700% spike), suggesting potential disruption in waste collection or accumulation of uncollected refuse.
evidence: Residential Disposal Complaint: 8 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly average (z-score: 5.04, 276% spike)
Sanitation Worker or Vehicle Complaint: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.77, 700% spike)
Unsanitary Condition remains top complaint category overall (441 over 90 days), indicating persistent sanitation concerns
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if there were route disruptions, staffing shortages, or service changes 2-3 weeks ago
Visit high-complaint areas to assess current trash accumulation and collection frequency
Interview residents about whether complaints have subsided or if collection remains irregular

themes_detail.label: Construction Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: 298 new DOB building permits filed over the last 90 days (181 alterations, 63 new buildings) correlate with elevated complaints about construction noise (12 THIS WEEK, up 182%) and general street disruption, suggesting rapid construction activity may be impacting quality of life without adequate community notice or enforcement.
evidence: 298 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (181 alterations, 63 new buildings)
General Construction/Plumbing complaints: 12 THIS WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly average (182% spike)
5 active SNAD/zoning applications in pipeline (5204 Arlington, 5294 Sycamore, 4695 Independence, etc.)
Community Board repeatedly requests traffic/pedestrian safety improvements, suggesting construction-related impacts are chronic concern
reporting_angles: Profile recent permit activity and identify which neighborhoods are seeing most construction—do complaints cluster geographically?
Examine whether SNAD applications and active permits align with complaint hotspots
Interview community board about whether developers are providing adequate community notice and whether permit enforcement is adequate
